transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Kim (Redwood AE), Marina Lopez (Redwood SE), Ravi Srinivasan (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO - Harborline), Elena Burke (Head of Security), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Nadia Ruiz (Legal)

Summary (auto):
Intro, quick qualification of hosting preferences (hosted vs dedicated vs private), deep dive on security controls: SOC2/ISO posture, SSO (SAML) integration, RBAC model, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS options, and data residency. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 materials, infra diagram, schedule a dedicated pilot run.

Topics: SOC2 compliance, SAML SSO integration, customer-managed KMS, RBAC scoping, audit log retention, private deployment network requirements

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:05] Jesse Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jesse with Redwood. Quick round robin — could you tell us what you're looking to validate from an infosec side today?
[00:00:18] Samir Patel: Yeah hi, Samir here. We're evaluating options to host inference for our AML and fraud models. Security is table stakes — SOC2 first, and then we need to know SSO, KMS, audit logs, retention. Basically can you run in our VPC and give us strong controls.
[00:00:35] Elena Burke: And to add — we have regulatory constraints in UK and some EU customers; data residency matters. Also, legal will want to see retained logs for 90 days minimum.
[00:00:48] Jesse Kim: Totally. Marina, do you want to walk through the hosting options and where the controls sit?
[00:00:52] Marina Lopez: Sure. So Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem). For Hosted the control plane is multi-tenant but we provide tenant isolation, encryption at rest, and SOC2 reports — we can do SAML SSO via SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC is configurable at the team and token level. For Dedicated you get isolated GPU pools and can pick private networking between the models and your VPC. Private is full customer-managed control plane – that maps more to on-prem or air-gapped needs, which seems relevant if you need full control of keys.
[00:01:27] Liam O'Connor: When you say 'SCIM for user provisioning', can we map our existing groups to roles? We have a security group that should only be allowed to call live models, while a separate dev group should only call staging endpoints.
[00:01:40] Marina Lopez: Yes, you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. There are some pre-defined roles but we can create custom ones during the pilot. Sometimes the mapping is a little clunky with different IdP attribute names — we've seen Okta and Azure AD differences, and SAML metadata can get misread sometimes — but it's solvable.
[00:01:56] Elena Burke: Ok we use PingFederate. Any known issues?
[00:02:00] Marina Lopez: Ping is supported; we typically ask for the SAML metadata XML and the x509 cert. Occasionally the NameID format needs a tweak. We'll include troubleshooting steps in the SSO doc.
[00:02:13] Jesse Kim: On encryption — do you require customer-managed KMS? We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) in Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted we can support CMEK via cloud KMS in certain regions.
[00:02:29] Samir Patel: We prefer CMK for production. We need a key rotation policy and HSM-backed keys. What's your compromise for Hosted?
[00:02:36] Ravi Srinivasan: For Hosted we can enable CMEK in supported cloud regions — the keys would live in the customer's KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault) and Redwood will have access as an IAM principal that you can rotate. For Dedicated and Private you can deploy the runtime with KMS integration that never exposes plaintext to Redwood control plane. Note: some customers deploy Dedicated in a VPC peering model where telemetry and metrics still route to Redwood for observability; if you want no telemetry leaving your VPC we can discuss an offline ops model.
[00:03:05] Nadia Ruiz: Legal question — if logs are routed, how do you handle PII in traces?
[00:03:10] Marina Lopez: Great question. We have configurable redaction on request payloads, and the platform can hash or truncate tokens. We also support token scrubbing in logs, and you can elect not to send request/response bodies in telemetry if you're running Private.
[00:03:25] Elena Burke: For audit logs — format and retention? We need immutable logs for 90 days and export ability to our SIEM.
[00:03:33] Marina Lopez: Audit logs include user actions (token creation, model deploys, rollouts), API requests, and admin events. We write them to append-only storage and can stream to your syslog or S3 bucket. Retention is configurable; Hosted default is 30 days, we can extend to 90 or more as a paid add-on. The export to your SIEM is typically through S3 or syslog forwarding and we can push to Splunk or Datadog.
[00:03:54] Liam O'Connor: Do logs include request/response payloads?
[00:03:57] Marina Lopez: By default, no — we log metadata and hashes for tracing. Full payload logging is opt-in and can be disabled for regulated workloads.
[00:04:07] [00:04:10] Samir Patel: On SOC2, do you have Type II? Auditors will want to see the last report, plus your change control docs.
[00:04:17] Jesse Kim: We have a SOC2 Type II, latest report was 2026-06. We'll send a redacted copy and a control mapping. We also have an ISO 27001 certification in progress — expecting audit completion Q4 but we can provide the scope.
[00:04:30] Nadia Ruiz: Can you share your incident response playbook and the SLA around data breaches?
[00:04:35] Marina Lopez: We have an IR playbook and a 48-hour initial response SLA for critical incidents for enterprise customers. For Dedicated customers we can negotiate faster RTO objectives.
[00:04:46] Elena Burke: For dedicated pool — do you run hypervisor-level telemetry? I'm trying to understand attack surface.
[00:04:52] Ravi Srinivasan: Our Dedicated topology uses containerized runtime on bare-metal/GPU hosts. We instrument kernel events for resource isolation and eBPF-based network monitoring in the cluster — but that telemetry doesn't include customer payloads. The runtime manages KV cache and model weights separately. If you require, we can run the control plane outside your network while the serving nodes remain in your VPC.
[00:05:17] [00:05:20] Liam O'Connor: What's the network flow for a VPC Private deployment? Do we open ports to Redwood or is it outbound-only?
[00:05:25] Marina Lopez: Normally it's outbound-only for agent communication, but for metrics ingestion we ask for an egress to our metrics endpoint. For stricter air-gapped setups it's all outbound/proxy through your egress with a pinned TLS cert. We'll share the network port checklist.
[00:05:40] Jesse Kim: Let's talk retention and deletion. If Harborline needs to delete data for a user or region, what's the workflow?
[00:05:47] Elena Burke: Right — data subject requests, data residency.
[00:05:50] Ravi Srinivasan: We support deletion APIs and can run a jurisdictional wipe for dedicated/private deployments. For Hosted, deletions are supported but there is a short window where cache or backups might persist; we provide a documented SLA for deletion. If you need guaranteed immediate irrevocable deletion we recommend Private or Dedicated.
[00:06:09] Samir Patel: For our use case, we want PII scrubbed and tokenization before anything leaves our environment. Is that something Redwood supports at the SDK or proxy level?
[00:06:18] Marina Lopez: Yes — you can run a preprocessing proxy in your VPC to strip or tokenize PII before sending to Redwood. We also have client SDK hooks for local redaction.
[00:06:28] [00:06:30] Nadia Ruiz: On contract terms — indemnity around data breaches and subprocessor lists?
[00:06:34] Jesse Kim: We have a standard subprocessor list and can provide DPA language. For enterprise deals we can negotiate indemnity and liability caps.
[00:06:42] Elena Burke: Can you talk about RBAC granularity — can we prevent model rollouts by engineers unless security approves?
[00:06:48] Marina Lopez: Yes, we have role gating on deploys, you can require approvals for production rollouts and set canary policies; RBAC integrates with SAML groups and you can add an approval workflow.
[00:06:58] [00:07:01] Samir Patel: Any benchmarking or performance tradeoffs when enabling CMEK or more aggressive logging?
[00:07:06] Ravi Srinivasan: CMEK introduces a tiny latency for key fetch on session creation, usually sub-10ms, and caching reduces that. Logging can add overhead if you stream full payloads — that's why we recommend hashing and metadata-first logging for low-latency paths.
[00:07:20] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot we'd like to validate throughput at our 200 RPS peak and P50 latency under 120ms for short prompts. Can Redwood dedicate a pool for that?
[00:07:29] Jesse Kim: Yes, a dedicated reserved pool for the pilot is typical. Marina will draft the pilot plan.
[00:07:36] Marina Lopez: I'll propose a 7-day bench with a 4-GPU pool, synthetic load, and a shadow traffic run from your production mirror. We'll also include security checks: SAML integration, KMS key usage traceability, and audit log export.
[00:07:50] [00:07:53] Nadia Ruiz: On data exportability — if we switch providers how easy is it to get model logs, prompts, and embeddings out?
[00:07:58] Marina Lopez: You can export logs and stored artifacts; for embeddings we store vectors and you can request a bulk export. For Hosted we maintain a retention window, but for Dedicated/Private you control storage and exports directly.
[00:08:12] Samir Patel: Anything else we should be aware of security-wise?
[00:08:16] Marina Lopez: A couple of gotchas: prefix caching can leak correlations if not scrubbed — we recommend aggressive token-level redaction for any PII. Also, function/tool calling features require attention to outbound connectors — those are disabled by default in Private.
[00:08:32] Elena Burke: Good to know.
[00:08:34] [00:08:40] Jesse Kim: Let's recap and assign owners — we'll send SOC2 and an ISO scope note, Marina will send the pilot plan and network checklist, and Samir will share SAML metadata. Marina, any docs we should attach?
[00:08:51] Marina Lopez: I'll attach: SOC2 stub, SAML integration guide, RBAC mapping template, KMS integration notes, network port checklist, and sample DPA language.
[00:09:03] Liam O'Connor: Can you include an estimated cost ballpark for a 4-GPU pilot and ongoing dedicated capacity?
[00:09:09] Jesse Kim: I'll include a rough cost table — ballpark for pilot and a monthly committed rate for dedicated pools.
[00:09:16] Nadia Ruiz: We'll need legal to review DPA and indemnity in the next two weeks.
[00:09:20] Jesse Kim: Understood.
[00:09:23] [00:09:25] Marina Lopez: Ok I'll draft and send by Monday.
[00:09:28] [00:30:00] [long silence while sharing screens, demos, and doc URLs — transcript picks up spots]
[00:30:05] Marina Lopez: (screen share) here's the SAML mapping, note the attribute mapping can be custom — ping us if group claims are blank.
[00:30:21] Samir Patel: Looks good. On the KMS side, we will want HSM-backed keys and a rotation schedule of 90 days.
[00:30:29] Ravi Srinivasan: Rotation of 90 days is fine; we log key usage events and can surface them to your SIEM.
[00:30:35] Elena Burke: Do you expose key usage events with principal identity?
[00:30:40] Marina Lopez: Yes, we log the principal (service account or user) that requested decryption and the resource id. Those are included in the audit export.
[00:30:48] [00:30:55] Samir Patel: Final question — what happens if Redwood has a region outage? Can we auto-failover to another region with data residency constraints?
[00:31:02] Jesse Kim: We have multi-region fallbacks but they depend on your residency policy. For strict residency, failover is limited; for others we can route to a nearby region. We'll document the options and recommended fallback policy.
[00:31:16] Elena Burke: Great.
[00:31:18] [00:31:20] Jesse Kim: Thanks everyone — we'll send the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff for next week.
[00:31:26] Samir Patel: Thanks team, appreciated.
[00:31:29] Nadia Ruiz: Thank you.
[00:31:31] Marina Lopez: Thanks all.

End of call.
